issues.original: Ethernet is a wired networking connection. Wi-Fi uses radio and supports mobility but may suffer interference. Bluetooth suits short-range links such as a nearby keyboard or headphones, considering power and bandwidth. Choose connections from the actual range, mobility and throughput requirements.
issues.printed: Ethernet is wired. Wi-Fi is wireless and mobile, but may suffer interference. Bluetooth suits short-range links. Compare speed and range.

issues.original: Layers separate communication responsibilities and provide services through agreed interfaces. One component can be changed while keeping its interface, without redesigning every layer. This supports compatible implementations, independent development and fault isolation. You do not need to memorise the names and functions of all TCP/IP layers for J277.
issues.printed: Protocol layers separate jobs through agreed interfaces, making changes and troubleshooting easier. OCR J277 does not require all TCP/IP layer names.

issues.original: Locked server rooms, controlled entry and secure equipment restrict physical access. They reduce theft and tampering opportunities. A password alone does not stop someone entering a server room or stealing an unprotected device; combine appropriate physical and logical measures.
issues.printed: Physical security uses locked rooms and controlled entry to reduce theft or tampering. Combine this with digital protection such as passwords.

issues.original: A constant is a named value intended to remain unchanged during execution, such as MAX_CLASS_SIZE=30. A variable such as score changes. Integer stores whole numbers; real can store fractional values such as 2.75. A character is one character such as a middle initial; a string is a sequence such as a full name.
issues.printed: A constant stays fixed (MAX_CLASS_SIZE=30); a variable may change. Integer=whole number; real=fraction; character=one; string=several.

issues.original: A Boolean stores true or false. For example, complete=false is a Boolean state; it is different from the string "false". Comparisons such as score>=50 produce Boolean results that can be combined using AND, OR and NOT.
issues.printed: Boolean values are true or false, not text strings. Comparisons such as score>=50 also yield Boolean results and combine with AND/OR/NOT.

issues.original: A local variable or constant is accessible within its defining local scope. A global variable or constant has wider program scope. Constants are intended to stay fixed during execution; variables may change. Unnecessary mutable global state makes unintended changes harder to track.
issues.printed: Local variables/constants belong to local scope; global ones have wider scope. Too much mutable global state makes bugs harder to trace.

issues.original: A function may receive an array as an argument, process it and return an array result. For example, receive [2,4,6], create a new array by adding 1 to each element, then return [3,5,7]. The caller must use the returned result. Passing the input and returning the output are separate actions; the original changes only if the implementation changes it.
issues.printed: A function can receive an array argument, process it and return a result. Input and return are separate; the caller must use the result.
